title: Reactive tracking sensitivity starting range
summary: For reactive tracking, a good starting range is about 28-35 cm/360 because the category often benefits from faster answer speed while still demanding controlled finishes.
why: Viscose explicitly describes playing reactive tracking in a higher range, usually around 28-35 cm/360.
Reactive tasks need you to physically answer fast strafes quickly enough, but still decelerate into a controlled track.
actions: Start around 32 cm/360 and test a little faster if you can read the strafe but cannot answer in time.
If your corrections are noisy or you keep overshooting the finish, slow down slightly inside the range.
Track whether the new sensitivity changes your tension or lockout more than your raw score.
avoid: Do not choose speed alone if the finish quality becomes unstable.
Avoid using the fastest possible setting just because the scenario is reactive.

drills.label: Reactive tracking sens sweep
drills.reason: Reactive tasks make it easier to feel the tradeoff between answer speed and correction noise.

evidence.claim: Reactive tracking is usually played around 28 to 35 cm/360, sometimes a bit faster.
evidence.excerpt: I tend to play these scenarios at a higher sensitivity compared to control tracking. Anywhere from 28 to 35 cm per 360.
